the controllability index of deformation is a new concept, and the controllability is higher in polycrystals than in single crystals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the controllability index is an important material attribute that is distinct from the conventional mechanical properties such as strength and ductility.
, for a given material, the MCI is determined by the material microstructures, and the MCI can be increased by reducing the volume of the materials.

MCI provides a quantitative measure of the controllability in mechanical deformation.
a small-volume material with a high MCI can be shaped precisely, while one with a low MCI would be difficult to shape precisely.
